text:
jenn.l: Quick heads-up: POC with LedgerEdge is blocked. They can resolve our private hostname but TLS fails during handshake when routed through their corporate egress proxy. They want a demo tomorrow.

omar.s: what error are they seeing? any curl/openssl snippets? which cloud/region?

jenn.l: region: azure-eastus2, Private Link. They sent this curl output: 
```
curl -v https://rdw-private.ledger.svc --resolve rdw-private.ledger.svc:443:10.2.3.8
* Connected to rdw-private.ledger.svc (10.2.3.8) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11)
* SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

They also ran openssl: 
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.3.8:443 -servername rdw-private.ledger.svc -showcerts
verify return:1
depth=0 CN = rdw-private.ledger.svc
depth=1 CN = Redwood Intermediate CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```

rachel.b: sounds like intermediate not served by the endpoint or the proxy is stripping the chain. If their proxy enforces TLS inspection, it will present its own cert which won't match our chain. Ask for `dig +short rdw-private.ledger.svc` and a full `curl -vI` to capture headers.

jenn.l: dig shows `10.2.3.8`. curl -vI (with --resolve) returns `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and a header `Via: corporate-inspect-1`.

omar.s: that `Via` header confirms interception. Two paths: 1) security approves passthrough for our destination (simplest), or 2) we provide a cert chain they trust (signed by their internal CA) OR 3) deploy a small Redwood Private gateway inside their VNet to terminate TLS locally and egress to our control plane over a managed tunnel.

rachel.b: option 2 requires them to share their internal CA root or let us issue a cert they can import into their proxy. That has compliance implications. Option 3 is heavier but often wins for enterprise POCs.

jenn.l: they're pushing back on importing CAs. Security insists on interception but will consider a per-host allowlist for a short window. They asked if we can support a short-lived demo using a public endpoint + IP allowlist so they don't have to change proxy rules.

omar.s: we can spin up a temporary public endpoint bound to a customer-dedicated hostname and restrict by source IPs. Fastest demo, but note: not everyone accepts public endpoints due to data controls — document that as an exception.

eng-bot: Created support ticket SPT-7896: "LedgerEdge POC - TLS fail via corp egress proxy; options: public demo endpoint / customer cert / private gateway". Assigned to eng-infra; ETA: 1 business day for public-demo spin, 3 business days for gateway estimate. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SPT-7896

rachel.b: jenn, please confirm whether they prefer (A) quick public-demo + IP allowlist, (B) share internal CA / cert import for proxy, or (C) proceed with Private gateway estimate. Also flag pricing delta for gateway.

jenn.l: i've asked security for option A approval first. if denied, will push for gateway estimate. Will update when i hear back. thanks team :thumbsup:

omar.s: one more diagnostic if they can run it from a workstation behind the proxy: `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.3.8:443 -servername rdw-private.ledger.svc -status` and paste full output including any proxy TLS cert details (subject/issuer). That helps us know if it's our cert missing or proxy cert being injected.

jenn.l: noted. will collect and post output. timeline pressure but looks solvable.

rachel.b: also prepping a short checklist for customers using Azure Private Link: DNS conditional forwarding, Private DNS zone linking, ensure NAT rules allow OCSP/CRL egress, and preferred: enable TCP passthrough for demo endpoints. I'll attach in SPT-7896.

jenn.l: awesome, thanks. will relay checklist and proposed options to LedgerEdge now.
